preamble: The voiced retroflex fricative [ʐ] (the Mandarin r- initial) became the lateral [l] in several northern Mandarin varieties, usually before the rounded vowel u. In Jinan (Jilu Mandarin) the change is regular in that environment: ʐ stays in 日 [ʐʐ̩] 'sun', 熱 [ʐə] 'hot' and 人 [ʐẽ] 'person', but became l in 如 [lu], 入 [lu], 辱 [lu], 軟 [luã] and 弱 [luə]. Harbin (Northeastern Mandarin) has l beside ʐ in the same u-syllables (如, 入, 辱), and Qingdao (Jiaoliao) has 辱 [lu]. Wikipedia, citing Ting (1991), reports that central Jiangsu Lower Yangtze Mandarin (including Yangzhou) merged /ʐ-/ with /l-/ in all environments.

examples.note: Before the rounded vowel u, the r- initial is l in Jinan; before unrounded vowels it is still ʐ (日 [ʐʐ̩21] 'sun').
The l- and ʐ- readings coexist; l- is found only before u, while 人 [ʐən24] and 日 [ʐʐ̩53] keep ʐ.
